summary: Oliver Philipp Frey works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna, where he served as a Predoc Assistant from 2013 to 2016, and was an SNSF Postdoc.Mobility Fellow at Savitribai Phule Pune University (2023–2025).

Olivia Cattedra specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She has held positions at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (research officer, attested 2007), Colorado College (Associate Professor, attested 2008), and the National University of Mar del Plata (attested 2011).
Olivia Porter works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at King's College London until 2023 and became a Teaching Fellow at the University of Leeds in 2025.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and Faculty of Arts of Paris under Lévi, Maritain, Masson-Oursel, and Bloch, he held posts at Ankara, Lille, EPHE, Paris, and ICI.

Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Pierre L. Lamant. He was affiliated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 1991 and has served as Professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Copenhagen, Harvard, and Washington under Tord Olsson, Karl H. Potter, Collett Cox, and Christian Lindtner, he held affiliations at Lund University and the University of London.

Olli Littunen specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed a BA at Leiden University (2016–2022) and has pursued doctoral studies there under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Olof August Danielsson (1852–1933) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Uppsala under Axel Erdmann and in Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and Bruno Lindner, later serving at Uppsala University as Docent and Professor.

Om Prakash works in Indology and history/archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma and Bisheshwar Prasad, later teaching at the University of Delhi, Kirori Mal College, and the Delhi School of Economics.
Omkar Supekar works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under J. L. Shaw in 2023 and has been a Research Scholar at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (attested 2025).

On Shionoya (1878–1962) was a sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1899–1902) and the University of Leipzig (~1906–1909). He later held an academic post at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1920 to 1938.
Ondřej Novák (1946–1977) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He completed his undergraduate studies (1965–1969) and earned his Ph.D. (~1969–1975) at Charles University.

Onorio Ferrero de Gubernatis Ventimiglia (1908–1989) worked in Indology and taught Oriental languages and cultures at the National University of San Marcos (~1948–1980) and the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru (1952–1976).

Oreste Nazari (1866–1923) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Gaspare Gorresio (~1886–1891). He taught at the University of Turin (~1900–1923) and served as a professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Palermo (1901–1923).
Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He was also a teacher of Shenphen Nangwa.
Oriane Lavolé works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She has been a doctoral student and PhD candidate at Stanford University, with posts and studies attested in 2020 and 2026.

Orion Klautau works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed a B.A. at the University of São Paulo and a Ph.D. at Tohoku University, where he served as Associate Professor in 2015.

Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, David P. Jackson, and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at Hamburg, NGMRP, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Osamu Hayashima (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg, later holding professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.
